title: Use operator-reported Aviva visibility when Fortna/non-UPS users lack Aviva access
summary: When you (support) cannot access Aviva directly, use an operator who can view Aviva to report what they see. Capture those operator-reported Aviva observations as evidence for later diagnosis, and use RMS as the first-step system-fault check during the call.
when_to_use: Use during an issue call when you need Aviva observations but you do not have direct Aviva access (described as typical for non-UPS/Fortna users).
not_for: Do not assume Aviva state without operator-reported evidence when you lack access.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Confirm whether you have Aviva access; if not, coordinate with an operator who can view Aviva and capture their observations for diagnosis.
Operator: View Aviva and report what is visible to support (what to look at and what they are seeing).
access_or_tools_needed: RMS screen access (for the first-step check, per source)
Support note-taking to capture what the operator reports from Aviva

access_required: Access to the RMS screen (for the first-step check)

visual_references.description: Aviva access limitation guidance and call flow: non-UPS users lack Aviva access; use an operator to look in Aviva; first step is to check RMS system faults.
RMS described as the robot management system web application (context for RMS screen usage).
RMS page description including system faults on the left and active AGV faults on the right (used to ground the 'first step' RMS fault check).

steps.title: Confirm whether you have direct Aviva access
steps.purpose: Determine whether you can directly observe Aviva or must rely on an operator to provide Aviva evidence.
steps.instruction: During the issue call, determine whether you (as the support user) have access to Aviva. The source states that non-UPS/Fortna users generally do not have access to Aviva.
steps.expected_result: You determine that you either have Aviva access or you do not have Aviva access (and therefore need operator-reported Aviva observations).
steps.healthy_condition: If you do not have Aviva access, you proceed to identify an operator who can view Aviva.
steps.failure_condition: You proceed as if you have Aviva visibility without confirming access, or you attempt to diagnose Aviva state without operator-reported evidence.

actions.label: Check Aviva access availability
actions.exact_action: Confirm whether you (as the support user) have access to Aviva

stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot confirm Aviva access, do not assume Aviva state; use operator-reported evidence instead.

steps.title: Identify an operator who can view Aviva
steps.purpose: Get Aviva observations from someone who has Aviva visibility when support lacks direct access.
steps.instruction: If you do not have Aviva access, identify an operator who can look at Aviva and report what they are seeing.
steps.expected_result: An operator is available who can view Aviva and provide observations to support.
steps.healthy_condition: Operator confirms they can view Aviva and is ready to report what is visible.
steps.failure_condition: No operator with Aviva visibility is available.

actions.label: Request operator Aviva visibility
actions.exact_action: You'll have an operator who you can tell where to look in Aviva to tell you, you know what they're seeing.

stop_or_escalate_if: If no operator with Aviva visibility is available, escalate to a role that can access Aviva or otherwise obtain the required Aviva evidence.

steps.title: Tell the operator where to look in Aviva and what to report
steps.purpose: Ensure the operator captures the specific Aviva evidence needed for diagnosis.
steps.instruction: Direct the operator to the relevant area(s) in Aviva and ask them to report what they see. Use the operator as your Aviva observation source when you cannot access Aviva directly.
steps.expected_result: Operator provides Aviva observations (what is visible in Aviva) that can be recorded as support evidence.
steps.healthy_condition: Operator reports concrete Aviva-visible information (not assumptions) that matches the area you instructed them to check.
steps.failure_condition: Operator cannot provide Aviva observations, or reports information without checking the Aviva screen.

actions.label: Instruct operator where to look in Aviva
actions.exact_action: Tell where to look in Aviva to tell you, you know what they're seeing.

stop_or_escalate_if: If operator cannot provide Aviva evidence, do not proceed with Aviva-based conclusions; escalate or obtain alternative evidence.

steps.title: Capture operator-reported Aviva observations in support notes
steps.purpose: Preserve Aviva evidence for later diagnosis and troubleshooting steps.
steps.instruction: Record the operator’s Aviva observations as part of the support notes for later diagnosis.
steps.expected_result: Support notes contain operator-reported Aviva observations that can be referenced during follow-up diagnosis.
steps.healthy_condition: Notes clearly attribute the Aviva observations to the operator’s view (what they saw) and include enough detail to interpret later.
steps.failure_condition: Notes are missing Aviva observations or contain assumptions not supported by operator-reported evidence.

actions.label: Document operator Aviva observations
actions.exact_action: Record the operator’s Aviva observations as part of the support notes for later diagnosis.

stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot capture operator-reported Aviva observations, do not proceed with Aviva-based diagnosis; escalate or obtain alternative evidence.

steps.title: Use RMS as the first-step check during the call
steps.purpose: Follow the source call-flow guidance: check RMS system faults first, since support may not access Aviva.
steps.instruction: During the call, go to the RMS screen first and check for any system faults.
steps.expected_result: You have checked the RMS screen for system faults as the first step on the phone call.
steps.healthy_condition: RMS system faults are reviewed (source describes system faults on the left and active AGV faults on the right).
steps.failure_condition: You skip the RMS first-step check and rely on Aviva evidence without RMS fault review.

actions.label: Check RMS system faults
actions.exact_action: go to that RMS screen, see if any system faults

success_criteria: Operator-reported Aviva observations are captured in support notes despite lack of direct Aviva access.
RMS system faults are checked as the first step during the call.
healthy_conditions: Support does not attempt to access Aviva directly when access is not available; instead, operator reports what they see in Aviva.
RMS system faults are reviewed on the RMS screen during the call.
failure_conditions: No operator with Aviva visibility is available and Aviva evidence cannot be obtained.
Aviva state is assumed without operator-reported evidence when support lacks access.
RMS system faults are not checked as the first step on the phone call.
escalation_guidance: If no operator with Aviva visibility is available, escalate to a role that can access Aviva or otherwise obtain the required Aviva evidence.
